title: Argus — Observability
description: Argus service health: HTTP RED metrics, scheduled polling, per-feed health, the ingestion pipeline, deduplication, data quality, JVM, PostgreSQL and HikariCP, container resources, Tempo traces and Loki logs. Version-controlled in grafana/dashboards and validated by the Argus dashboard tests.

list.name: source
list.label: Source
list.description: Filters the ingestion, deduplication, data-quality, fetch-retry and 304-ratio panels by feed source.

list.name: feed
list.label: Feed
list.description: Reserved for per-feed series; All only for now.

list.name: level
list.label: Log level
list.description: Filters the live log stream by level.

panels.title: Target up
panels.description: Scrape targets for the Argus job that Prometheus currently reaches. 0 means Prometheus cannot scrape the service (it may still be running). Shows 0 when the target does not exist at all.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Seconds since the JVM started. A value that keeps resetting means restart loops (OOM kills, failed health checks).

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Server-side failures as a share of all requests. The error count falls back to 0 when no 5xx series exists yet, and clamp_min avoids dividing by zero when the request rate is 0. The panel is empty until the first request is served.

panels.title: p95 latency (excl. stream)
panels.description: 95th percentile request latency, leaving out the long-lived /news/v2/stream connections. Shows no traffic when nothing was requested in the window.

panels.title: Last poll age
panels.description: Seconds since the last completed poll, even if some feeds failed in it. Shows never until the first poll after a restart. Orange from 15 minutes and red from 30 minutes mean the schedule has stopped running.

panels.title: Feeds enabled / failing
panels.description: Count of enabled and failing feeds. A feed is failing when consecutive failures reach or exceed the failing threshold (default 3).

panels.title: New articles 24h
panels.description: Total articles inserted into the database in the trailing 24 hours across all feeds.

panels.title: Poll duration
panels.description: Duration of feed polling runs: p95 by trigger and max duration by trigger.

panels.title: Poll outcomes
panels.description: Polling runs per second by trigger and outcome. completed: the poll ran to the end, even if some feeds failed in it (see Feed health). failed: the poll itself threw, for example the feed list could not be read. interrupted: shutdown cut the poll short; feeds that had finished stay stored.

panels.title: Retries by source
panels.description: Rate of transient HTTP fetch retries per second grouped by feed source.

panels.title: 304 ratio
panels.description: Share of fetches that ended in 304 Not Modified, meaning the feed had not changed since the stored validators were sent. Low values on feeds that publish rarely mean the validators are not being honoured. Filtered by the source variable.

panels.title: Feed health
panels.description: One row per feed: state, consecutive failures and time since the last successful fetch (including 304). Failures are orange from 1 and red from 3, the default failing threshold. Since last success is orange from 1 hour and red from 6 hours; never means the feed has not succeeded since it was added. Click a row for its logs in Loki.

panels.title: Stalest feeds
panels.description: The five feeds with the longest time since their last successful fetch (including 304). A feed that has never succeeded reports -1, which would sort last, so the query lifts it to a sentinel value that sorts first and shows as never. The bar is full from one day.

panels.title: Permanent redirects by outcome
panels.description: Permanent (301/308) redirects the poller met, per second by outcome. permanent_applied: the feed's stored URL was moved to the redirect target. permanent_conflict: the target already belongs to another feed, so this feed was disabled as a duplicate (see its Loki WARN line).

panels.title: Identity conflicts by kind
panels.description: Feed create or update requests rejected because the URL matches another feed, per second by the kind of match: entered (the submitted URL), redirect (a permanent redirect target) or self_link (the feed's own declared URL).

panels.title: Fetch outcomes
panels.description: Fetches per second by outcome and reason. Failures carry the reason tag (for example timeout, http_status, io); successful fetches have reason none. Empty until the first feed is added or refreshed.

panels.title: Fetch p95 by source
panels.description: 95th percentile time to fetch a feed, per source. Includes failed fetches. Empty until the first feed is added or refreshed.

panels.title: Ingest p95 by source
panels.description: 95th percentile of an ingest run per source. A refresh covers fetch, parse and persist; the first ingest after POST /feeds covers persist only.

panels.title: Bytes per fetch
panels.description: Mean response size per successful fetch, by source, from the fetch size summary. The denominator is clamped so the panel stays defined when nothing is fetched.

panels.title: Entry decisions
panels.description: Parsed entries per second by persist decision: inserted, updated, linked, unchanged or skipped. Stacked so the total is the entry throughput.

panels.title: Skip reasons
panels.description: Rate of skipped entries per second by reason (missing_identity, batch_duplicate).

panels.title: Link-fallback outcomes
panels.description: Rate of link-fallback outcomes per second (guid_replaced, guarded_homepage, guarded_shared).

panels.title: Lock wait p95 by source
panels.description: 95th percentile duration waiting for per-source advisory transaction locks during ingest.

panels.title: Updates by reason
panels.description: Rate of updated entries per second by update reason: content_changed, timestamp_only (also used when an entry matched an article first seen through another feed of the source and its upstream update time is newer) or insert_conflict (the article already existed under that GUID, this feed was linked to it and its content left untouched).

panels.title: Duplicate pressure
panels.description: Share of entries that are duplicates (linked or unchanged) relative to total entries seen.

panels.title: Cross-feed overlap
panels.description: Share of cross-feed duplicate links relative to new content (inserted or linked). A linked entry matched an existing article first seen through another feed of the source, unless its upstream update time is newer (then it counts as updated{timestamp_only}).

panels.title: Source merges: rate and p95
panels.description: Source merges and feed moves per second by type (merge or feed_move), and their 95th percentile duration. Merges are rare, so gaps are normal. The p95 is on the right axis.

panels.title: Collapsed articles by type
panels.description: Duplicate articles removed by a source merge or feed move over each interval, by type (merge or feed_move). Zero means the run found no duplicates.

panels.title: Missing fields rate
panels.description: Entries per second that arrived without a field, by kind of field. A rise points at a feed that stopped providing it.

panels.title: Missing fields share
panels.description: Share of entries missing a field, by kind. The denominator is every entry seen by the decision counter (argus_ingest_entries_total) and is clamped, so the panel stays defined at zero traffic.

panels.title: Job runs by outcome
panels.description: Scheduled poll runs by outcome. success: the poll completed. skipped: the previous poll was still running. error: the poll failed unexpectedly, so look at the logs. interrupted: shutdown cut the run short, which is expected during a deploy. A flat line means the schedule has stopped.

panels.title: Request rate by route
panels.description: Requests per second by URI template and method. Unmatched routes appear as NOT_FOUND.

panels.title: Latency quantiles
panels.description: p50, p95 and p99 request latency, excluding /news/v2/stream. Gaps mean no traffic in the window.

panels.title: Status mix
panels.description: Requests per second by HTTP status code.

panels.title: Heap used vs max
panels.description: Heap in use against the configured maximum. Used approaching max means GC pressure and a coming OOM exit.

panels.title: GC pause
panels.description: Time spent in garbage-collection pauses per second, by cause.

panels.title: Live threads
panels.description: Live JVM threads. A steady climb points to a thread leak.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Process CPU usage against whole-host CPU usage, as a fraction of capacity.

panels.title: Pool connections
panels.description: Hikari pool connections: active, idle, pending (threads waiting for one) and the configured maximum. Pending above zero means the pool is saturated.

panels.title: Connection acquisition p95
panels.description: 95th percentile wait to borrow a connection from the pool. Gaps mean no acquisitions in the window.

panels.title: pg_up
panels.description: Whether the PostgreSQL exporter can reach the database (1 up, 0 down). Needs the postgres-exporter job.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size of the argus database as reported by the PostgreSQL exporter.

panels.title: Commits and backends
panels.description: Transaction commits per second and open backend connections for the argus database, from the PostgreSQL exporter.

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: Populated only where cAdvisor runs (the real Swarm stack); empty on the local verification stack. CPU cores used by the argus service.

panels.title: Container memory
panels.description: Populated only where cAdvisor runs (the real Swarm stack); empty on the local verification stack. Working-set memory of the argus service.

panels.title: Slow and errored traces
panels.description: TraceQL search for Argus traces that errored or took longer than 1s. Open a trace for the waterfall; from a span, Logs for this span pivots into Loki.

panels.title: Log volume by level
panels.description: Log lines per level over time. Of the JSON log fields, only level is promoted to a Loki label; use the level and search variables to narrow the stream below.

panels.title: Live log stream
panels.description: Argus log lines filtered by the level and search variables. Of the JSON log fields, only level is promoted to a Loki label. Each line's traceId becomes a link to Tempo through the Loki datasource's derived field.
